questions.stem: What does Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) cover?
options: Where data comes from and where it goes
The process from where data was generated until it is removed from the systems
The monetary valuation of data assets
The matching of records across systems
The parallel processing of queries
questions.explanation: DLM is about the whole process from the point where data is generated until it is removed from the systems.

questions.stem: How does Data Lifecycle Management differ from Data Supply Chain?
options: DLM is a technology; Data Supply Chain is a process
DLM covers generation to removal; Data Supply Chain covers where data comes from and where it goes
DLM applies only to structured data; Data Supply Chain only to unstructured data
They are the same thing under two names
DLM is for OLTP; Data Supply Chain is for OLAP
questions.explanation: The two are often confused: DLM spans generation to removal, whereas Data Supply Chain describes where data comes from and where it goes.

questions.stem: What does the Data Generation step of DLM refer to?
options: The channel where data is generated, such as a mobile application, CRM, ERP, CCTV, social media or emails
The business rules that transform raw data
How long data is kept
The criteria for deleting data
How transformed data is matched with raw data
questions.explanation: Data Generation means the channel through which data originates, for example mobile apps, CRM, ERP, HRM, CCTV, social media, audio, emails and documents.

questions.stem: What does the Data Processing step of DLM describe?
options: The business rules by which raw data is transformed into the required format, via ETL, ELT, data mining or machine learning modelling
The reports and dashboards on which data is shown
The means by which data is extracted
The channel in which data originates
The criteria on which data is removed
questions.explanation: Data Processing covers the business rules used to transform raw data, whether via ETL, ELT, data mining or data science machine learning modelling.

questions.stem: Which DLM step covers how transformed data is matched with raw data, shown on reports and dashboards, and what it was used for?
options: Data Generation
Data Processing
Data Reconciliation, Presentation and Utilisation
Data Storage Lifespan and Extraction
Data Removal
questions.explanation: The Reconciliation, Presentation and Utilisation step addresses matching transformed data to raw data, presenting it, and recording the purpose it served.

questions.stem: What does the Data Storage Lifespan and Extraction step of DLM define?
options: The transformation rules for raw data
The channel that generated the data
How long the data will be kept and the manual or automated means of extracting it
How data discrepancies are found
The frequency of dashboard refreshes
questions.explanation: This step specifies for how long data will be kept and what the means of extracting it are, whether manual or via automated tools.

questions.stem: What does the Data Removal step of DLM record?
options: Which reports used the data
How data was encrypted
Which department owns the data
How data has been removed and on which criteria
Which model was trained on the data
questions.explanation: Data Removal means how data has been removed from the systems and based on which criteria.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the DLM steps listed in *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: Data Generation
Data Processing
Data Removal
Data Storage Lifespan and Extraction
Data Valuation
questions.explanation: The DLM steps are Generation, Processing, Reconciliation-Presentation-Utilisation, Storage Lifespan and Extraction, and Removal; Data Valuation belongs to Data Due Diligence.

questions.stem: Which of these is given as an example of a data generation channel in DLM?
options: A star schema
A semantic layer
An OLAP cube
A CCTV camera
A data mart
questions.explanation: CCTV is listed among the generation channels, alongside mobile applications, CRM, ERP, HRM, social media, audio, emails, documents, images and scans.

questions.stem: Which transformation approaches are named under the Data Processing step of DLM?
options: Referential, probabilistic and ML association
JDBC, ODBC, native drivers and APIs
Landing, staging and transformed zones
COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX
ETL, ELT, Data Mining or Data Science Machine Learning Modelling
questions.explanation: Raw data may be transformed via ETL or ELT, or via Data Mining or Data Science Machine Learning Modelling.
